function: DDPG learns the RIS phase-shift matrix that raises the rate of wanted V2V links and suppresses unwanted ones, reshaping the topology for decentralized FL (p. 1, 7).
system: Single-antenna flying cars (8 nodes), passive reflecting RIS with 30-70 elements, TDMA V2V links, 3 MHz bandwidth; carrier frequency not stated (p. 4, 10).
method: DDPG reinforcement learning for RIS phases, trained offline (p. 8); MobileNet/DenseNet perception models trained with decentralized federated learning (p. 9).
data_channel: Custom simulator: quasi-static flat Rayleigh fading (Table I: Rice factor 10), LoS/NLoS path loss; 5000-image multiview vehicle dataset for the FL task (p. 6, 9, 10).
test_conditions: DDPG trained on the 8-car platoon of Fig. 5, RIS size 30-70, no unseen scenario reported; FL test set is the held-out 30% of the data (p. 9-10).
baselines: Direct analytic RIS control and no-RIS (non-learned, p. 10-11); no earlier learned RIS controller; FL: initial topology, ring-based DFL, centralized FL, no FL (p. 11-12).
metrics: Link transmission rate (Mb/s), DDPG reward, tolerable delay and weight convergence, perception accuracy of MobileNet/DenseNet, training time per epoch (p. 9-12).
complexity: Measured training time per epoch versus RIS elements (Fig. 14): under 0.25 s below 30 elements, about 4 min for 1000 epochs, RTX 2060 GPU (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 6: "quasi-static flat-fading Rayleigh channel". Table I (p. 10) lists Rice factor 10 and LoS/NLoS loss coefficients: custom simulator, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured channel is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 9: "the test set is the remaining 30% of the view data set". The DDPG is trained for the 8-car platoon of Fig. 5; dynamic topologies appear only as a flowchart (p. 8, Fig. 7) with no results, so no unseen scenario is tested.
q3_support: p. 10: "We design a direct RIS control algorithm to demonstrate the effectiveness of DDPG algorithms". This is the only non-learned RIS baseline; no earlier learned RIS controller (such as DQN) is compared. Ring-based DFL and centralized FL (p. 12) compare FL topologies on accuracy, not a learned RIS control.
q4_support: p. 11: "the training time of each epoch is less than 0.25 s. The total training consumption of 1000 training epochs is approximately 4 min"
q5_support: p. 9: "coded with PyTorch". No code or data link is given anywhere; the channel is simulated and the multiview vehicle images (p. 9) have no link or citation.
notes: Judgment call for the reviewer: the paper frames the RIS as network-layer topology control (p. 1, 6), but the learned part only outputs RIS phase shifts from link rates (p. 7) and the target topology comes from closed-form criteria (Theorem 1, p. 5), so I take it as area 3, not above_phy. DFL aggregation is digital peer-to-peer (p. 2, 4), not over the air, so not area 7. Text says Rayleigh (p. 6) but Table I lists Rice factor 10 (p. 10). q4 rests on training time per epoch (p. 11), not inference time. One antenna per car (p. 4) but a RIS is present, so the system check passes.
